title: `bucket` ignores a validator that happens to be falsy
spec:
This is the more-itertools library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`.

I use a callable object as the `validator` for `bucket`: a `set` subclass with `__call__` that accepts only the keys it contains. When that set is empty the validator is ignored and every key is accepted.

```python
import more_itertools as mi
class AllowedKeys(set):
    def __call__(self, key):
        return key in self

D = mi.bucket([10, 20, 11, 21], key=lambda x: x, validator=AllowedKeys())
10 in D         # expected False, actual True
list(D[10])     # expected [], actual [10]
sorted(D)       # expected [], actual [10, 11, 20, 21]
```

The docs say the validator decides which keys are valid. Any callable passed as `validator` should be used as given, whatever its truth value; only leaving it out (`None`) should mean "accept every key".
acceptance: The reported example gives the expected results for `in`, selection and iteration
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
